note_en: To say how well something is done, Chinese puts 得 after the verb and the evaluation after 得: 把工作做得更好 "do the work better." English uses an adverb ("better," "well"); Chinese uses this "degree complement" instead. When the verb has an object, 把 moves the object up front so the verb can sit right next to 得: 把工作 + 做得更好.
